title: ～にくい — “hard to ～”
summary: Added to the ます-stem of a verb, にくい means that something is hard to do. It describes the nature of an object, tool or situation that makes the action difficult. It works like an i-adjective, so it conjugates as one.

patterns.form: 動詞ます形の語幹 ＋ にくい
patterns.gloss: 飲む → 飲みにくい / 読む → 読みにくい / 歩く → 歩きにくい

patterns.form: 〜にくかった／〜にくくない／〜にくいです
patterns.gloss: Conjugates like an i-adjective: 読みにくかった, 読みにくくない

body.p: Add にくい to the ます-stem of a verb (飲み, 読み). にくい is a suffix meaning “difficult,” and the whole word becomes an i-adjective. The opposite is やすい (飲みやすい, 読みやすい).

Use it when the nature of a thing or situation makes an action hard: the medicine is bitter and hard to take, the writing is small and hard to read, the new shoes are hard to walk in. It pairs well with ～て and ～ので to give the reason.
When the difficulty comes from a person's ability or feelings, use 難しい or づらい rather than にくい. にくい describes the nature of the object or tool itself.

examples.ja: この薬（くすり）は苦（にが）くて飲（の）みにくいです。
examples.romaji: Kono kusuri wa nigakute nomi nikui desu.
examples.tr: This medicine is bitter and hard to take.

examples.ja: この字（じ）は小（ちい）さくて読（よ）みにくい。
examples.romaji: Kono ji wa chiisakute yomi nikui.
examples.tr: This writing is small and hard to read.

examples.ja: 新（あたら）しい靴（くつ）はまだ歩（ある）きにくい。
examples.romaji: Atarashii kutsu wa mada aruki nikui.
examples.tr: The new shoes are still hard to walk in.

pitfalls: Attach it to the ます-stem, not the dictionary form: 飲みにくい, not 飲むにくい.
The negative is ～にくくない; 飲みにくじゃない is wrong.
